paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the classification accuracy (%) achieved by various models on novel real-world classification tasks, as reported in the paper "LaSQuE: Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning." The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 40% to 65% in 5% increments, with a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists the different models being compared, arranged from left to right in the following order: RoBERTa w/o Exp. (light gray), ExEnt (light blue), LaSQuE (mean) (orange), LaSQuE (green), LaSQuE (syn2real) (purple), and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) (dark gray). Each model is represented by a single, solid-colored bar, with no grouping or stacking. The approximate accuracy values for each model are as follows: RoBERTa w/o Exp. achieves around 47%, ExEnt reaches approximately 55%, LaSQuE (mean) is about 49%, LaSQuE (green) is approximately 49%, LaSQuE (syn2real) attains around 58%, and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 62%. The bars are not sorted by performance but appear to follow a logical progression of model variants, with the most advanced model (including curriculum learning) positioned on the far right. No additional annotations, error bars, or statistical significance indicators are present.
